If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture upward momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, apply a 3–5% downward correction to mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecast to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (±0.3) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to late-horizon (16–30 days) forecast to account for momentum carryover.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.5% from late-horizon forecast to avoid overcorrection from prior negative momentum.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.5) and forecast deviates >3% from true path, apply a 1–2% smoothing correction to mid-late horizon to dampen volatility from sentiment noise.
